newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Brunei to sign US$1 bln refinery agreement.
newsitem.headline: Brunei to sign US$1 bln refinery agreement.

text.p: Brunei on Wednesday will sign a memorandum of understanding with Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) and Japan's Kanematsu Corp to build a US$1 billion refinery and petrochemical complex, officials said.
CPC chairman Lee Shu-chiu arrived in Brunei on Sunday and has met government officials and toured Brunei Shell's oil and refinery installation in the sultanate, a CPC official in Brunei said.
Brunei Shell's complex is the sultanate's only refinery.
The new complex would include a 60,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery to process Brunei's crude oil.
The complex would include an aromatics plant to produce and export 420,000 tonnes of paraxylene a year and 200,000 tonnes of benzene a year.
The plan represents another move by the sultanate to expand its energy sector away from reliance on crude production.
Brunei produces 165,000 bpd of crude oil, most of which is exported. It has a small 9,000 bpd refinery serving its population of 270,000.
In May, Brunei signed a letter of intent to build a 160,000 bpd refinery at a cost of $1.5 billion with state-owned German engineering group IAB.
